breakfast.name: Pulaka (Giant Taro)
instructions: Boil pulaka until tender
Serve with coconut cream
breakfast.description: Boiled giant taro with coconut cream.

breakfast.name: Fried Fish and Rice
instructions: Cook rice
Fry fish
Serve together

breakfast.name: Pawpaw (Papaya) with Lime
instructions: Ripe papaya with lime juice is the Pacific island breakfast
The papaya is sweet and perfumed
The lime cuts the sweetness and adds brightness
Simple, fresh, and tropical
Papaya grows readily on Pacific islands
breakfast.description: Tuvaluan tropical fruit breakfast -- ripe papaya with fresh lime juice. The papaya is sweet and perfumed; lime cuts the sweetness. Papaya grows readily on Pacific atolls. Simple and fresh.

breakfast.name: Coconut Porridge
instructions: Coconut milk porridge is the Tuvaluan breakfast
Oats or tapioca cooked in coconut milk
The coconut milk replaces the water -- richness and flavor
Sweetened simply
breakfast.description: Tuvaluan coconut milk porridge -- oats or tapioca cooked in coconut milk instead of water, sweetened simply. Coconut milk enriches everything in Pacific island cooking.

lunch.name: Fish and Coconut
instructions: Simmer coconut cream
Add fish, cook 15 min
Add lime and onion

lunch.name: Pork and Breadfruit
instructions: Brown pork
Add breadfruit and coconut milk
Simmer until tender
lunch.description: Pork and breadfruit in coconut milk.

lunch.name: Pulaka (Giant Taro)
ingredients: Pulaka (Cyrtosperma merkusii -- the large swamp taro grown in Tuvalu)
instructions: Pulaka is the Tuvaluan staple crop -- a giant swamp taro grown in pits
Cyrtosperma merkusii: the swamp taro -- larger, starchier, and more calorie-dense than regular taro
Grown in babai pits: excavated coral pits filled with compost and freshwater
Tuvalu's fresh water is extremely scarce -- the babai pit system conserves it
Boiled or baked with coconut milk
Climate change threatens pulaka cultivation -- saltwater intrusion from rising seas contaminates the freshwater pits
lunch.description: Tuvaluan giant swamp taro -- pulaka (Cyrtosperma merkusii), grown in babai pits (excavated coral pits with freshwater and compost). Tuvalu's freshwater is scarce; the babai system conserves it. Boiled or baked with coconut milk. Climate change and rising seas contaminate the freshwater pits with salt.

lunch.name: Palusami (Taro Leaves in Coconut Cream)
instructions: Palusami is the pan-Pacific taro leaf and coconut cream dish
Young taro leaves folded around thick coconut cream and onion
Wrapped in banana leaves
Cooked in an umu or steamed
The taro leaves soften completely -- they become silky
The coconut cream absorbs into the leaves
Eaten across Samoa, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Fiji
lunch.description: Tuvaluan taro leaf parcels -- young taro leaves wrapped around thick coconut cream and onion, enclosed in banana leaves and cooked in an umu or steamed. The leaves become silky as they absorb the coconut cream. Palusami is eaten across Samoa, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Fiji.

lunch.name: Fish with Coconut Sauce
ingredients: Fresh fish (tuna, snapper, or flying fish)
instructions: Fish is the primary protein in Tuvalu
Tuvalu sits in the middle of the Pacific -- surrounded by ocean
The Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) is much larger than the land area
Fish cooked in coconut cream is the simplest and most common dinner
The cream softens and enriches the fish
Tuna is the main commercial fish species in the Tuvaluan EEZ
lunch.description: Tuvaluan coconut cream fish -- fresh tuna or snapper gently cooked in coconut cream with lime and onion. Fish is the primary protein: Tuvalu's ocean EEZ is far larger than its land. Tuna dominates the Tuvaluan commercial fishery.

dinner.name: Laulau (Wrapped Fish)
instructions: Wrap fish with coconut cream in leaves
Bake or steam 30 min

dinner.name: Coconut Crab
instructions: Cook crab in coconut cream
Serve with lime

dinner.name: Umu Feast
instructions: The umu (earth oven) is the Tuvaluan and wider Polynesian cooking method for feasts
Volcanic stones heated in a fire
Food wrapped in leaves placed on the stones, covered and steamed
The umu is opened for celebrations: Sunday meals, weddings, funerals
In Tuvalu (a coral atoll): the umu uses coral rubble stones -- volcanic stones are imported or improvised
The opening is an event: the smell of the leaves and steam is part of the ceremony
dinner.description: Tuvaluan earth oven feast -- coral stones heated by fire (volcanic stones are scarce on atolls), food wrapped in taro and banana leaves placed on the stones, covered and steamed 2-4 hours. Opened for Sunday meals and celebrations. The opening is a ceremony.

dinner.name: Baked Breadfruit
instructions: Breadfruit is a staple food across the Pacific islands
A whole breadfruit is baked directly over coals or in the umu
The skin chars and the inside becomes soft, starchy, and slightly sweet
Eaten with coconut cream
Captain Bligh of the Bounty was transporting breadfruit plants when the mutiny occurred (1789) -- he was trying to bring breadfruit from Tahiti to the Caribbean as a cheap food for enslaved people
dinner.description: Tuvaluan baked breadfruit -- whole breadfruit baked over coals until the skin chars and the starchy interior is soft and slightly sweet, eaten with coconut cream. Captain Bligh was transporting breadfruit plants from Tahiti to the Caribbean (for enslaved people's food) when the Bounty mutiny occurred (1789).

dinner.name: Octopus in Coconut Milk
instructions: Octopus is a regular Pacific island seafood
In Tuvalu, caught in the shallow reef areas
Cooked simply in coconut milk
The octopus becomes tender from the gentle braise
Served with rice or taro
dinner.description: Tuvaluan reef octopus in coconut milk -- octopus caught in shallow reef waters, braised in coconut milk with garlic and ginger until tender. Served with rice or taro.

snacks.name: Baked Breadfruit
instructions: Roast over coals 45 min
Peel and serve

snacks.name: Coconut Cream Drink (Koko)
ingredients: Mature coconut (grated and pressed for the cream)
instructions: Fresh coconut water and cream are the Tuvaluan drinks
Young coconut: the water is drunk fresh
Mature coconut: grated and squeezed for thick cream -- drunk as a rich snack
The coconut is the Tuvaluan pantry: drink, food, fat, vessel, and fiber
snacks.description: Tuvaluan fresh coconut -- young coconut water drunk fresh; mature coconut grated and pressed for thick cream. The coconut is the Tuvaluan pantry: drink, food, cooking fat, and vessel. Everything comes from the coconut.

snacks.name: Banana (Various Preparations)
ingredients: Bananas (various types -- plantain, cooking banana, sweet banana)
instructions: Bananas and plantains grow on Pacific atolls
Eaten raw when ripe
Cooked when green: boiled, baked, or fried
A reliable calorie source on atolls with limited agricultural land
Multiple varieties: some are starchy (cooking), some are sweet (eating)
snacks.description: Tuvaluan everyday banana -- multiple types grown on atolls: sweet bananas eaten raw, starchy plantains boiled or baked. A reliable calorie source on land-scarce Pacific atolls.

snacks.name: Crab (Coconut Crab or Land Crab)
ingredients: Coconut crab or land crab (freshly caught)
instructions: Coconut crabs are native to the Pacific islands -- Tuvalu has them
The world's largest land arthropod: Birgus latro
Climbs coconut trees to eat coconuts -- hence the name
Caught at night (they are nocturnal)
Boiled or steamed -- the meat is sweet and coconut-flavored
Their numbers have declined from over-hunting on many islands
snacks.description: Tuvaluan coconut crab -- Birgus latro, the world's largest land arthropod, native to the Pacific. Climbs coconut trees; nocturnal. Caught at night and boiled or steamed. The meat is sweet with a coconut flavor. Numbers have declined from overharvesting on many islands.

desserts.name: Coconut Candy
instructions: Cook coconut and sugar until thick
Drop onto tray
Let harden

desserts.name: Sweetened Taro (Taro Pudding)
instructions: Sweetened taro mashed with coconut cream is the simple Tuvaluan dessert
Cooked taro mashed until smooth
Coconut cream and sugar stirred in
Warm or chilled
A nourishing, simple sweet
desserts.description: Tuvaluan sweetened taro pudding -- cooked taro mashed smooth with coconut cream and sugar. Warm or chilled. A simple, nourishing dessert from the island's staple starch.

desserts.name: Coconut Candy
instructions: Coconut candy is the simple Pacific island sweet
Grated coconut mixed into caramelized sugar
Set into bars or pressed into shapes
A simple confection from the most available ingredient
desserts.description: Tuvaluan coconut candy -- fresh grated coconut mixed into caramelized sugar, set into bars. A simple confection from the most abundant Pacific atoll ingredient.

drinks.name: Toddy
instructions: Collect sap from palm
Drink fresh or let ferment

drinks.name: Coconut Water
instructions: Crack open, drink

drinks.name: Toddy (Coconut Sap)
ingredients: Coconut flower sap (tapped from unopened coconut flower spathes)
Optional: ferment for several days for alcoholic toddy
instructions: Coconut toddy is the tapped sap from coconut flower spathes
Fresh toddy: sweet, slightly fizzy -- drunk within hours of tapping
Fermented toddy: left 2-3 days -- becomes alcoholic
The tapping: a skilled Tuvaluan will climb the palm and carefully incise the flower spathe
The sap drips into a container over hours
Toddy tapping is a traditional Tuvaluan skill
Used to make sweet drinks, vinegar, or alcoholic beverages
drinks.description: Tuvaluan coconut palm toddy -- sap tapped from unopened coconut flower spathes. Fresh: sweet and slightly fizzy (drink within hours). Fermented: 2-3 days, mildly alcoholic. Tapping requires climbing the palm and incising the spathe: a traditional Tuvaluan skill. Also used as vinegar.
